Obstacle-Avoidance Mobile Robotic Rover

Explore AICORE's completed mobile robotic rover demonstrating obstacle sensing, embedded decision logic, motor control, and direction adjustment.

A working mobile robotic rover that detects nearby obstacles and adjusts its movement using onboard sensing, embedded decision logic, and motor-drive electronics.

Objective: Demonstrate obstacle-aware autonomous movement on a compact mobile robotic platform.

System overview: Obstacle sensors feed the embedded controller. The controller evaluates the readings, selects a movement response, and commands the motor driver to adjust the rover's direction.

Status: Completed Prototype. A working technical prototype implemented and demonstrated by AICORE. It is presented as engineering evidence, not as a production-certified commercial robot.

AICORE contribution: Mobile robotic-platform integration, Obstacle-sensor interfacing, Embedded decision logic, Motor-drive control, Movement behavior, Prototype integration and testing.

Capabilities demonstrated: Obstacle detection, Sensor-driven direction adjustment, Embedded decision logic, Motor-drive control, Mobile-platform integration, Prototype testing.

Technologies and system elements: Embedded control, Obstacle sensing, Motor-drive electronics, Mobile robotics.

Demonstrated results: The completed rover demonstrated mobile movement with onboard obstacle detection. The platform adjusted its direction in response to detected obstacles.

Limitations: The rover is not described as a SLAM, mapping, or production autonomous-navigation system. Range, speed, runtime, environmental rating, and field-deployment performance are not claimed.
